m1 - coordination answer sent to codex-storymodel-new-engineer (msg-01M16VGRY1B28Q07RB0RXGRFGW, corrected by msg-01M16VHVSYN072CKKPHSQX1GW2). No claim from me on this bead; the engineer should own it and I will review.

The constraints I own, recorded here so they are not only in a DM:

TEXT-AT-SPAN (4383a85): a unit's text must equal transcript.canonicalText at its span HULL. Hull rather than per-ref concatenation is deliberate - a unit spanning two sentences carries the gap material - and a test asserts the accepted text IS the hull slice so a later change to concatenation fails loudly.

THE GUARD THAT IS EASY TO LOSE: RecallGraph.validated ACCUMULATES rather than short-circuits, so the text check runs even on a graph whose span check has already failed. Without an explicit out-of-range guard the substring THROWS instead of refusing, and the mutation test proving that also protects a PRE-EXISTING span test. If the new constructor short-circuits, that guard becomes dead and its test starts passing vacuously - retire it deliberately rather than leaving it green and meaningless.

THE CODEC FOIL, where I differ slightly from the chief's framing. AlignCodecSuite's recall-checksum test builds an intentionally text-inconsistent graph and works today only because decode does not validate the supplied graph. Under a seal it becomes unconstructible. Chief suggested wire tampering OR a different valid recall; I would take THE DIFFERENT VALID RECALL. The property under test is "decode refuses a recall whose checksum does not match the proof", and a genuinely different valid recall tests exactly that and is the scenario that actually occurs; wire tampering tests a different property and would quietly change what the test means.

MEASURED MIGRATION SURFACE (I asserted this before checking, then measured it): 21 fresh `RecallGraph(` occurrences against 33 `.copy(units|transcript|relations)` sites in tests. The COPY surface is the larger half. Only two production constructors, both segmenters. The riskiest site is laws/AlignGens.scala - a generator, where a fallible constructor is most likely to be papered over with a .get or a silent filter, and a filter that discards is how a property suite stops testing the hard cases without saying so.

SHAPE PREFERENCE: private PLAIN class, not a case class with a private constructor. A case class still derives Mirror.ProductOf and its public fromProduct rebuilds the type field by field without consulting the constructor - demonstrated on PlacementResolution, where fromProduct built masses summing to 3.0 with a threshold of -5.0 while `of` rejected the identical values.
